content:
Maya: quick heads-up  noticed another burst of model churn this morning on /v1/complete where auto-fallback toggled between `rwd-8` and `rwd-8-quant` five times in 2m. users saw spikes of 502s and noisy alerts. proposal: add a per-route "churn suppression window" (temporary anti-churn) that blocks additional automated swaps for a short period after a decision. default 30s, configurable. keeps things stable. thoughts?

Kevin: big +1. couple of design concerns: fixed window vs progressive backoff vs circuit-breaker semantics. I prefer half-open probe semantics: after window expires allow one probe request to evaluate candidate before re-enabling automated swaps. Also need to dedupe identical back-and-forth flips (same two model ids).

Tara: console perspective: surface a small amber chip next to the route: "Suppression: 00:26". actions: "Extend" and "Force swap (reason required)". Force should open a modal requiring a reason and an opt-in to notify on-call. Also include a condensed swap timeline and a link to the decision trace.

Eli: infra plan: decision records get `suppression_until` timestamp + `probe_allowed` boolean + `swap_attempts` sliding counter. policy fields: `suppression_ms`, `probe_after_ms`, `max_swaps_window_ms`, `decay_factor`. Emit structured events: `suppression.started`, `suppression.probe`, `suppression.forced` with metadata {route, from_model, to_model, cause}.

Maya: telemetry: sample rich KV & request traces during probes at a tiny rate (0.5%) to aid debugging without huge cost. expose metrics: `suppression.active_count`, `suppression.probe_rate`, `model_churn_rate` per-route. audit logs must record suppression start, extensions, and operator overrides with actor and reason string.

Kevin: tests: e2e harness that replays jittery 5xx/latency bursts and asserts: no more than one automated swap per suppression window; probe behavior works; metrics increment. unit tests for sliding-window swap counting and decay behavior.

Tara: microcopy: avoid words like "lockout" or "throttle" which sound severe. suggested label: "Suppression (anti-churn)" tooltip: "Temporarily reduces automated model changes to prevent oscillation. Operators can force a swap with justification." For force modal require 20-char minimum reason and show last 5 fallback events.

Eli: API surface: decision-service returns `suppression_state:{active:true, remaining_ms:26000, probe_allowed:false, cause:"p95_latency"}` so console and dedicated/private planes can surface it. Add sandbox flag `simulate-suppression` for QA.

Maya: ops/compliance: ensure audit entries include operator id, timestamp, and reason text. retention consistent with rollout audit logs and searchable in console. Also redact PII in reason text if detected.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary plan -> `churn-suppression-v1` -> rollout 5% traffic on 2025-11-20T09:00Z. Monitoring: `suppression.active_count`, `model_churn_rate`, `fallbacks_per_min`.

Kevin: one more feature idea: `shadow_probe_pct` to route a tiny fraction (0.1-1%) to the candidate model during suppression for human review without affecting decisions. config per-route.

Tara: UI task: I'll add the chip, force modal mock, and a help panel "Why is churn suppressed?" linking to decision trace and sampled shadow logs. modal will have a checkbox to notify the on-call rotation.

Eli: draft proto snippet in PR: `message ChurnSuppression { int64 suppression_ms = 1; int64 probe_after_ms = 2; double shadow_probe_pct = 3; repeated string triggers = 4; }` will iterate after RFC.

Maya: plan: I'll write a short RFC today covering the policy schema, console visuals, telemetry, and tests. sync Fri 09:30 infra/design/qa. If no objections I'll start the RFC now :thumbsup:
